source.title: Successor Heads: Recurring, Interpretable Attention Heads In The Wild
source.authors: Rhys Gould; Euan Ong; George Ogden; Arthur Conmy

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether interpretable features recur across models, using SAE-derived mod-10 feature structure rather than a general representation-distance measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports successor heads across architectures and model sizes, but does not measure whether alignment between models rises with scale or compare distances between the same inputs. Its cross-model SAE feature results bear on V5. Other reported results, such as within-model task performance, are not rows for the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether the same interpretable circuit (successor heads) and features (SAE mod-10 features) recur across language models of different architectures and sizes. That is V5's claim. It uses circuit and SAE analysis rather than the original sources' methods.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors claim a weak universality: successor heads arise across architectures and scales (31M–12B) and use similar mod-10 features 'in all cases'. However, the mod-10 SAE evidence is shown for only three models (Pythia-1.4B, Pythia-2.8B, a GPT-2 Medium variant), not all models with successor heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study identifies successor heads using effective OV circuits and analyzes mod-10 features with sparse autoencoders; it does not use a general cross-model representation-distance method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that mod-10 features do not interpret or steer the day and letter tasks well; the feature-level account also misses the successor head's greater-than bias.
record.problems: The cross-model feature evidence is narrow, concerning mod-10 structure in a small set of language models and numeric-token tasks. The model-specific cross-model plots are figure-based, with no reported uncertainty or quantitative measure of similarity between models. The paper also notes limitations of the mod-10 account on days and letters.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure recurrence of the same interpretable features across different models; within-model successor scores and feature analyses do not independently establish cross-model recurrence.

untested.parts: Successor heads appear from 31M to 12B parameters, but no cross-model alignment is measured, nor any increase in alignment with scale.
No comparison across seeds of the same architecture.
No mapping or stitching between models.

Recurrence is tested only for successor heads and mod-10 features, on numeric and ordinal tokens in GPT-2, Pythia and Llama-2. No other features, modalities, or quantitative feature-matching across models are tested.
No comparison of similarity measures or input sets.
No analysis of shared data or objectives as causes, or of plateaus.

missing.what: Highest successor score per model across GPT-2, Pythia and Llama-2 families (31M–12B) against the 0.5 cutoff, showing the circuit recurs. Some models fall below the cutoff, e.g. GPT-2 Large.
Roman-numeral successor scores across GPT-2 and Pythia (≥1B) models and Llama-7B. Most models generalize; Llama-7B does not.
Successor scores across training checkpoints for Pythia-70m, 1.4b and 2.8b and Stanford GPT-2 Medium-C, showing successor heads emerge in each model.

record.verdict_notes: The record omits the main cross-model circuit-recurrence result (Figure 2), which bears on V5 more directly than the two appendix SAE rows. Rows should be added for it. None of the evidence includes a quantitative cross-model similarity score or uncertainty. The paper does not test whether recurrence increases with scale.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure representation alignment or distance between models, nor whether alignment increases with model size or capability.
Does not compare vision and language models on paired images and captions.
Does not compare models trained from different initializations of the same architecture or test shared subspaces across seeds.
Does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment between models.
Tests recurrence of mod-10 feature structure in a limited set of language models; does not test recurrence of neurons or circuits broadly, or across modalities.
Does not compare representation similarity measures, settings such as neighbour count, or in-distribution with out-of-distribution similarity.
Does not separate effects of shared data or objectives from a common model of reality, or measure whether cross-model alignment plateaus.

relationships.condition: Successor heads across GPT-2, Pythia and Llama-2 (31M–12B); mod-10 SAE features in Pythia-2.8B and GPT-2 Medium (Stanford)
relationships.reason: The authors report mod-10 SAE bands in both models (r1, r2). Per the text, Figure 2 also shows successor heads above cutoff across the three families (not in rows).
relationships.display_finding: Successor heads exceeded the cutoff across GPT-2, Pythia and Llama-2, while mod-10 SAE bands appeared in both Pythia-2.8B and GPT-2 Medium.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Successor heads across GPT-2, Pythia and Llama-2 (31M–12B); mod-10 SAE features in Pythia-2.8B and GPT-2 Medium (Stanford)
source_check.reason: Appendix A.3 explicitly reports recurring mod-10 structure for r1 and r2 (Figures 14–15). Figure 2 and the introduction report successor heads across the named families and parameter range; this broader evidence lacks dedicated rows.

relationships.reason: Text, not rows: GPT-2 Large has no successor head (Appendix I, Fig. 2). Original Llama-7B's successor head does not generalize to Roman numerals (Fig. 16). Mod-10 features fail on days and letters.
relationships.display_finding: GPT-2 Large had no successor head, original Llama-7B's head failed on Roman numerals, and mod-10 features failed on days and letters.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Appendix I explicitly identifies GPT-2 Large as lacking a successor head. Appendix B.2 reports poor Roman-numeral generalization for original Llama-7B. Section 3.4 and Appendix E report that mod-10 features cannot steer Days and Letters. These text-based exceptions qualify the positive recurrence results.
